note: Cases feed lowered programs to the rule. Synthetic traits pin each branch of the reaching analysis: a direct os/getenv answer arm that compares the answered value passes; the same sign-in without the arm, an unguarded or unrelated or negated guard, and the failure answer are flagged; a chain passes only when guard propagates to it from an env-guarded answer arm and no unguarded transition names its event (a cycle with no guarded entry is flagged), and an event that is also listened has an outside source. The real-program-shape cases lower std-dev-personas (the shape the owner ruled the rule from) and the same program with its env arms removed.

program.name: std-dev-personas
program.description: std-dev-personas — sign in as a development persona against the local Firebase Auth emulator. Compose it with linkedEntity set to the app's identity entity: its rows are the personas. POST /api/hooks/personas answers 200 { success, personas, source } (every row with a non-empty id; source identity-entity, or none when there are no rows). POST /api/hooks/persona-sign-in with { id } makes that row an emulator user (uid = id, display name = name, every other non-null field but email a custom claim) and answers 200 { success, customToken, authEmulatorHost, projectId }, the token unsigned (alg none), which only the emulator accepts. A composed client may also ask by event (PERSONAS_REQUESTED, PERSONA_SIGN_IN_REQUESTED { id }) and read the same answers (PERSONAS_ANSWERED, PERSONA_SIGN_IN_ANSWERED); the sign-in token it carries is the emulator's unsigned alg-none token, accepted only by the local emulator, and this dev-only path is the one exception to tokens-never-in-payloads. Both answer 404 unless FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_HOST is 127.0.0.1:9099, so a deployment lists and signs in nobody; a body without an id is 400, an unknown id 404, a field named like a reserved token claim or an emulator refusal 500. The emulator calls go through the composed std-http-client trait PersonaHttp (127.0.0.1:9099 over plain TCP, net grant); its authorization header is the declared credential FIREBASE_AUTH_EMULATOR_OWNER (Bearer prefix), filled by the host at the send, so no token is written in the program.
